title: Simplified Montage Cryo-Electron Tomography
content: Cryo-electron tomography is the leading technique for the investigation of cellular architecture. In this method, samples are vitrified and imaged directly, revealing mesoscale biological ultrastructure in its “near-native” state. A major weakness, however, is the severely limited field of view of the resulting images. Luckily, this can be alleviated by collecting multiple overlapping images which are then stitched together in a process called “montage tomography”.
